chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Fear the injustice, for it would be a darkness on the Day of Judgement'.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of injustice according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith links the Prophet’s warning against injustice to the concept of 'zulmat' (darkness), illustrating how moral corruption obscures the soul’s perception of divine truth. In Shia tradition, this is often interpreted as both a literal eschatological state and a metaphor for the spiritual blindness caused by self-oppression or oppressing others. The emphasis on 'ittiqā' (fear/heedfulness) underscores the proactive spiritual discipline required to avoid this darkness.

en.hubeali:
Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Fear the injustice, for it would be a darkness on the Day of Judgement’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ibn abu ‘Umayr has narrated from certain individuals of his people from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘
Beware of doing injustice; on the Day of Judgment there will be much darkness.’”
